md:
### Centrifugal and roller pumps at a glance

| | Centrifugal | Roller |
|---|---|---|
| How it works | Non-occlusive; preload-dependent, afterload-sensitive | Occlusion set for each case |
| Flow reading | Always use with a flow probe | Under-occlusion gives false flow readings |
| Hazards | No tubing wear | Over-occlusion: spallation, tubing rupture, haemolysis |
| Blood handling | Believed better (conflicting evidence); limited arterial air embolism in a paediatric ex vivo model | More free Hb and less haptoglobin (review of 33 RCTs, heterogeneous) |
| Static charge | Avoids triboelectric charge | PVC in the pump segment generates triboelectric charge; use silicone there (IIa C) |
| Typical use | Long procedures; mandatory in MiECC | Suction, venting and cardioplegia; used if pulsatile flow is wanted |
| Recommendation | Centrifugal pump for expected longer CPB (IIa C); centrifugal arterial pumps for haemocompatibility and safety (IIa C) | None specific |

Source: summarised from the 2024 EACTS/EACTAIC/EBCP bypass guideline, sections 4.1, 5.5, 5.8 and 9.1, as given in this tab.
anchor: Review of 33 RCTs: more free Hb and less haptoglobin with roller pumps

md:
### Brain protection strategies for arch surgery at a glance

| Strategy | How | Targets | Safe duration and evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unilateral ACP | Via the axillary, innominate or a common carotid artery | Flow 10–15 mL/kg/min; right radial 40–80 mmHg | 30–50 min |
| Bilateral ACP | Add a balloon-tipped catheter in the contralateral carotid, usually with a left subclavian occlusion balloon | As for unilateral | 86 to more than 164 min; possibly better with an incomplete circle of Willis |
| RCP | Oxygenated blood up the SVC cannula after arrest | Jugular venous pressure 20 mmHg; flow 100–500 mL/min | Only 3–5% returns via the arch vessels; may flush debris. Against DHCA alone: stroke OR 0.66, operative mortality OR 0.57 |
| ACP against DHCA alone | | | Stroke OR 0.62, operative mortality OR 0.63 |
| DHCA alone | Deep hypothermia (14.1–20°C) | | 30–40 min; DHCA in 6% of acute and 2% of elective European cases |

Source: summarised from the 2024 EACTS/EACTAIC/EBCP bypass guideline, sections 10.1 and 10.2, as given in this tab.
anchor: ACP vs RCP: no difference in mortality or major neurological complications

md:
### Returning the residual circuit blood: options compared

| Option | What goes back | Evidence quoted |
|---|---|---|
| Unprocessed return | Whole circuit blood, in a bag or chased through the arterial cannula with Ringer's acetate | Ringer's chase against bag (RCT): better platelet function, less haemolysis, better haemostasis; same blood loss |
| Cell salvage | Red cells only; plasma discarded | Higher Hb, but more thrombin generation and fibrinolysis, lower platelets, longer clot formation; avoids discard, so less transfusion. Small trial (51): better Hb gain and free Hb washout |
| Ultrafiltration | Removes water-soluble components only | Against unprocessed (RCT, 200): no difference; other RCTs: lower early morbidity and transfusion, less drainage, higher Hb |
| Recommendation | Return the residual volume to minimise allogeneic transfusion (I C); processed return should be considered (IIa B) | |

Source: summarised from the 2024 EACTS/EACTAIC/EBCP bypass guideline, section 11.5, as given in this tab.

md:
### Mechanical valve anticoagulation at a glance

| Point | Figure or rule |
|---|---|
| Drug | Lifelong VKA (I A); DOACs contraindicated (III A): RE-ALIGN and PROACT Xa stopped early |
| Start | VKA with therapeutic UFH or LMWH bridging 12–48 h after implantation or when bleeding is minimal, usually within 24 h in ICU |
| Stop bridging | When the INR is in range on 2 consecutive tests |
| Thromboembolic risk | Peaks at about 1 month, stays raised for 6 months |
| Higher INR (target 3, range 2.5–3.5) | Severe hypercoagulable states, LVEF under 35%, mitral and tricuspid prostheses |
| Good control | Time in therapeutic range 70% or more; self-monitoring in trained patients (I A) |
| Add aspirin 75–100 mg | Symptomatic atherosclerosis (IIa B) or embolism despite adequate INR (IIa C, or raise the INR target) |
| Definite DAPT need | Triple therapy with clopidogrel for up to 1 month, then drop one; no ticagrelor or prasugrel |

Source: summarised from the 2024 EACTS perioperative medication guideline, part 4, as given in this section.
anchor: Adding ASA 75 to 100 mg reduces thromboembolism but increases major bleeding
